descriptionChirho: A noun denoting a bodily discharge or flux, used exclusively in the ritual purity legislation of Leviticus 15 to describe an abnormal genital emission that renders a person ceremonially unclean. Applied to both male discharge (Lev 15:2-3, 13, 15, 33) and female discharge (Lev 15:25-26, 28, 30, 33). All multilingual glosses uniformly point to the same medical/ritual concept: Arabic sayalan ('flow, discharge'), German Ausfluss ('discharge'), French ecoulement ('flow'), Korean heureum ('flow'), Spanish flujo ('flux'). The various prepositional and suffixed forms (zovo, mizzovo, zovah, mizzovah) are inflectional variants of the same single sense.
